system_overview: This is a model-checking configuration module for the Nano blockchain specification. It makes the abstract Nano specification amenable to finite model checking by providing a concrete hash function implementation, handling hash depletion gracefully, and defining a state view that removes hash ordering from state comparison. The module works around TLC's level-checking restrictions by overriding the hash calculation constant in the model configuration rather than directly in the module.
actors_and_components: Same as the Nano specification: network nodes with private keys maintaining distributed ledgers. This module adds a hash function mapping that tracks which block is stored at each hash, enabling a concrete implementation of hash calculation.
state_variables: Inherits all state variables from the Nano specification (last hash, distributed ledger, received blocks) and adds one additional variable: a hash function mapping from hashes to blocks (or the empty sentinel), which tracks the assignment of hashes to blocks as they are created.
initial_state: The hash function maps every hash to the empty sentinel (no blocks assigned). All inherited state from the Nano specification is initialized as in that specification.
actions: Inherits all actions from the Nano specification (genesis block creation, send, open, receive, and change representative block creation and processing). Adds a check before each step: if there are no undefined (unused) hashes remaining, the system stutters (takes no action) rather than failing. The hash calculation implementation finds an unused hash for each new block and updates the hash function mapping.
safety_properties: Type invariant: the hash function mapping maintains its declared type, and all Nano type invariants hold. Safety invariant: all Nano cryptographic invariants hold.
model_bounds: The hash set size controls the maximum number of blocks that can be created. Three configurations exist with increasing hash set sizes (three, four, and five hashes). All configurations use two private keys, two public keys, two nodes, and a genesis balance of three. The state view for model checking excludes the hash function and last hash variables, so states that differ only in hash assignment order are considered equivalent.
additional_assumptions: The hash function implementation assigns hashes to blocks on a first-available basis: when a new block needs a hash, it picks any hash currently mapped to the empty sentinel. If an existing block is rehashed, the same hash is returned. The key pair and node ownership mappings are chosen deterministically using bijective mappings between private keys and public keys, and between nodes and private keys. The set of private keys and public keys must have equal cardinality, and the number of private keys must not exceed the number of nodes. The module uses TLC's constant override mechanism to work around level-checking restrictions on variable-level hash functions.
